title: NNSA capacity hold: draft PEIS scenarios are analytical cases, not production results
summary: NNSA's draft PEIS analyzes multi-site capacities including 30 pits per year at LANL plus 50 at Savannah River, as well as higher maximum and lower capability-based scenarios, while acknowledging that months or years with no production may occur. Denominator: Environmental-analysis scenarios spanning 10 to 80 pits per year at LANL and 50 to 125 at Savannah River, not observed qualified output or accepted rate production.
key_findings: Evidence stage: Rate, capacity, and baseline hold.

Finding: NNSA's draft PEIS analyzes multi-site capacities including 30 pits per year at LANL plus 50 at Savannah River, as well as higher maximum and lower capability-based scenarios, while acknowledging that months or years with no production may occur.
Denominator: Environmental-analysis scenarios spanning 10 to 80 pits per year at LANL and 50 to 125 at Savannah River, not observed qualified output or accepted rate production.
Boundary: A draft environmental analysis is not a final production decision or operating result.
Boundary: Analyzed capacity is not installed, accepted, sustained, or used capacity.
Boundary: The scenarios do not provide a qualified output count, schedule confidence, lifecycle cost, or GAO-accepted program baseline.
Next action: Reopen only with final decisions plus installed and accepted capacity, recurring qualified output, period, site, rejects, rework, schedule, cost, and independent validation.
why_it_matters: The visible hold preserves a useful reporting, schedule, capacity, performance, or baseline boundary without presenting it as an accepted result.
